title: VOR / RMI / ADF Related Questions
src: R.K. Bali — Air Navigation, Part III Ch 5. Worked examples (Q2, 4, 7, 10, 11, 13, 19–22) turned into choices with the book's working as the answer; others keyed from the printed grid, PDF p. 262

qs.q: Flying towards the station on heading 330°, ADF showing 350°, CDI 2 dots fly left (5-dot), FROM showing. Which radial is the aircraft on?
qs.ex: MBT = 330 + 350 − 360 = 320, so the aircraft is on the 140 radial (the book's OBS works out to 136, reverse sensing).

qs.q: An aircraft is on a bearing of 263° (M) from a VOR station and the OBI is set to 091°. The deviation indicator will show:
On a true bearing of 230° from the station, heading 240° (M), mean variation 5° E. What does the ADF (co-located NDB) show?
An aircraft is on radial 120 with a magnetic heading of 300°; the OBS reads 330. The CDI shows "fly":
The OBI of a VOR is set to 090°. The TO/FROM indicator shows TO and the CDI needle is deflected halfway to the right. On what radial is the aircraft?
Flying towards the station on heading 210° with 10° starboard drift; CDI 2 dots fly left, FROM showing. What does the RBI (co-located NDB) show?
Flying from VOR A to VOR B on track 120°. Half-way, with the CDI showing 2 dots fly right, the pilot selects VOR B. The new indication will be:
o: FROM, and CDI 2 dots fly right
TO, and CDI 2 dots fly right
FROM, and CDI 2 dots fly left

qs.q: Inbound on radial 090°, the pilot rotates the OBS 10° to the left, turns the aircraft 10° right and notes the time. Holding a constant heading, the CDI centres in 8 min. In nil wind, the time and final heading to the station will be:
qs.ex: Turn 10° off and rotate the OBS 10°: an isosceles triangle, so the time to the station equals the time flown, 8 min; heading to the station 260°.

qs.q: Homing to the station on heading 045° (M) with 10° starboard drift; VOR and NDB co-located. What does the ADF show?
Flying away from the station with 10° starboard drift on true heading 300°, variation 5° E; VOR and NDB co-located. What does the ADF show?
ADF 170°, heading 030° (M), TO showing, CDI 2 dots fly right, DME 120 NM. How far is the aircraft off the selected track (2° per dot)?
The heading read on a standard RMI is:
An RMI shows aircraft heading. To convert the RMI bearings of NDBs and VORs to true bearings, the variation to apply is:
o: NDB: aircraft position, VOR: aircraft position
NDB: aircraft position, VOR: beacon position
NDB: beacon position, VOR: aircraft position

qs.q: If you correctly tune a VOT situated to your east, your RMI should read … and your OBS would read …
o: 090; 090 with needle central and FROM indicated
000; 000 with needle central and TO indicated
000; 000 with needle central and FROM indicated

qs.q: An RMI slaved to a remote-indicating compass has failed and is locked at 090°. The tail of the VOR pointer shows 135°. The available information from the VOR is:
Heading 180° T, variation 7° E. The ADF shows 200° relative; NDB and VOR co-located. What does the RMI show?
Homing to the station on heading 315° T, variation 5° W. The RMI shows 090°. What does the ADF (co-located NDB) show?
Heading 041° (M), 17.5 NM from a VOR, on magnetic bearing 215° from it; VOR and NDB co-located. What is the relative bearing?
The RMI shows 170° and the heading is 030° (M). What does the ADF read?
A VOR is tuned. With 049° on the OBS the deviation bar centres with TO showing. The aircraft's radial and heading to the station are:
Heading 230° (M), RBI shows 040°. What is the magnetic bearing of the aircraft from the NDB (variation 5° W at the aircraft, 6° W at the NDB)?
qs.ex: QDM = 230 + 040 = 270, so the bearing from the NDB is 090.

qs.q: The VOR system is limited to about 1° of accuracy. One degree at 200 NM represents a width of:
Heading 225° (M), ADF/RMI reading 090°. The quadrantal error of this bearing is:
o: proportional to sine heading times the signal strength
qs.ex: RB = 090 − 225 + 360 = 225: a quadrantal bearing, so the error is at its maximum.

qs.q: An aircraft is flying a constant heading with 8" right drift and is making good a track parallel to the center line of an airway but 5 nm off to the left of the center line. The ADF reading of a NDB on the airway center line 42 nm ahead of the aircraft is:
Heading 270° (M), OBS also 270°, full left deflection and FROM flag. In which sector from the VOR is the aircraft?
If the ADF pointer indicates 200 degrees when the RMI rose is stuck at 090 degrees, what is the relative bearing of the beacon?
On radial 240°, heading 230°, CDI 2 dots fly right, TO showing. What OBS is set, and what type of sensing?
Aircraft heading is 080 deg (M). OBS is selected to 060 deg. Aircraft is on a radial of 040 deg (M). To/from indication and CDI will show:
An aircraft is heading 055, RMI reading 060. After some time RMI reads 057 with no change of heading. Aircraft has drifted :
qs.ex: The QDM falls from 060 to 057 while the heading stays 055: the station moves left, so the aircraft is drifting right (starboard).
